answer: RESULT HANDOFF. Direct answer: all three symbolic-capital indicators (Zhausgr, ZDolch, ZAxtSchwert) load on PC1 (30.33% variance) with **the same sign and similar moderate magnitudes** (−0.23, −0.27, −0.30 post-alignment) — a tight same-sign cluster whose contribution to PC1 ranges from 5.1% (Zhausgr) to 8.9% (ZAxtSchwert). On PC2 (19.47% variance; cumulative 49.79%) the three indicators are **strongly asymmetric**: house size contributes a moderate positive loading (+0.33, ~10.7% of PC2), while daggers (+0.07) and hatchets/swords (+0.05) sit essentially at zero (0.55% and 0.29% of PC2 respectively). Across the 39 century slices, the PC2 score distribution is wide and slightly positive on average (range −3.70 to +2.54, range 6.23; median +0.34; IQR [−0.94, +1.05]; 59% of bins with PC2 > 0). All artifacts saved under artifacts/analysis and artifacts/data including the executed PCA script, full 12×12 loadings, per-BCE PC1..PC12 scores, focused symbolic-on-PC1/PC2 row-table, summary.json, run log, and findings.md (with the contract ≤8-sentence closing-paragraph hypothesis). Std-dev verification recorded (max|μ|=0.001, max|σ−1|=0.469 driven by ZSichel); re-standardized before PCA. Caveats: BCE 4100/4200/4300 are identical source rows (one pre-Neolithic baseline repeated 3×) which inflated the PC2 negative tail; sklearn was unavailable so PCA via numpy.linalg.svd on centered data (mathematically equivalent to sklearn.PCA(n_components=12)).

payload.hypothesis: In the PCA on the 12 forms-of-capital indicators across the 39 century bins (BCE 4300→500), the three symbolic-capital components — house size (Zhausgr), daggers (ZDolch) and hatchets/swords (ZAxtSchwert) — load on PC1 (30.3% variance, sign aligned so Pottery Form is positive) with the same sign and similar moderate magnitudes (−0.23, −0.27, −0.30; 5–9% PC1 contribution each), forming a tight co-varying cluster that distinguishes them jointly from the burial-display/pottery pole on the opposite end of the axis. On PC2 (19.5% variance; cumulative 49.8%) the three indicators are strongly asymmetric: house size carries a moderate positive loading (+0.33, ≈11% of PC2 variance) while daggers (+0.07) and hatchets/swords (+0.05) sit essentially at zero, so symbolic capital on PC2 is carried almost entirely by house size. Across the 100-yr slices PC2 scores are broadly dispersed — range [−3.70, +2.54] = 6.23 wide, median +0.34, IQR ≈ ±0.99, with 59% of bins (23 of 39) positive — exhibiting a slight positive central tendency and a strong negative outlier tail driven by the three identical deep-prehistoric bins (BCE 4300–4100). Synthesis: symbolic capital is unified and moderate on PC1, but split on PC2 — house size drives the secondary axis while daggers and hatchets/swords are quasi-orthogonal to it, so the "distribution along PC2" of symbolic capital effectively reduces to the house-size trajectory, which is itself widely spread but mildly positive across most century slices.
payload.workflow: 1) Load data/capital.csv (39×15), parse comma decimals → float in the 12 Z columns, drop group/color. 2) Verify pre-standardization: means ≈ 0 (max |μ|=0.00128) but stds unequal (min 0.53 for ZSichel, max 0.99); re-standardize each column to exact (mean 0, std 1) → 39×12 standardized matrix. 3) Run a single PCA via numpy.linalg.svd on the centered 39×12 matrix (sklearn unavailable; mathematically equivalent to sklearn.PCA(n_components=12)). 4) Sign-align per researcher: PC1 flipped so ZKeform loading is positive (raw = −0.3529 → flipped); PC2 sign aligned so largest-|loading| variable is positive (ZBeil at +0.4706 was already positive → no flip). 5) Extract full 12×12 PC1..PC12 loadings and per-PC1/PC2 contribution shares; produce focused row-table for Zhausgr/ZDolch/ZAxtSchwert. 6) Compute per-BCE-bin PC1..PC12 scores; characterize PC2 score distribution (min/max/range/median/Q1/Q3/IQR/frac_positive). 7) Save all artefacts (.py, .md, standardized matrix, loadings, scores, focused table, summary.json, run log) under artifacts/.
